summary: Palestine has no border control of its own — every route into the West Bank runs through Israeli-controlled crossings (Ben Gurion Airport or the Allenby Bridge from Jordan), so Israel's entry rules determine who gets in; the Palestinian Authority issues no visas, and Gaza is effectively closed to travelers.

passportValidity.text: Israel controls all crossings into the West Bank. Its Population and Immigration Authority requires a passport valid for at least 3 months from the date of arrival.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — About ETA-IL (eligibility conditions)

travelInsurance.text: Visa-exempt visitors entering through Israel on an ETA-IL are not asked for insurance. Applicants for Israel's eVisa-B2 tourist visa must show health insurance valid for the whole visit. Check that any policy covers the Palestinian territories, as many insurers exclude them.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — eVisa-B2 tourist visa: required documents

onwardTicket.text: Applicants for Israel's eVisa-B2 tourist visa must upload a round-trip ticket. The ETA-IL application for visa-exempt visitors does not ask for one, though Israeli border officials may ask detailed questions about your itinerary.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — eVisa-B2 tourist visa: required documents

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published. Applicants for Israel's eVisa-B2 tourist visa must prove sufficient funds with bank statements for the last three months, a bank letter or another document showing the funds.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — eVisa-B2 tourist visa: required documents

currencyLimits.text: Israeli rules apply at all crossings — cash of ILS 50,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be reported on entry.

source.name: Israel Tax Authority — Requirement to report money brought into or taken out of Israel

notes: The UK's travel advice, which covers Israel and Palestine together, says there are strict rules on goods you can take in or out, and points to the Israeli Tax Authority for the rules on carrying money.

The UK says visitors entering through Ben Gurion Airport get an entry card instead of a passport stamp (other crossings may stamp instead), and to keep the card with your passport until you leave, as you may need it when crossing into Palestine.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Palestine has no official currency of its own and that the Jordanian dinar, the Israeli shekel and the US dollar are all accepted. It says the West Bank's fragile banking system relies mainly on card payments for day-to-day transactions and that ATMs there may not accept foreign cards, while Gaza has no ATMs or banks and runs on cash only.

safety.text: Conditions differ sharply by area: Gaza is a war zone and closed to travelers, while the West Bank sees checkpoints, periodic military operations, settler violence and protests. Most governments advise against all travel to Gaza and urge heightened caution — or advise against travel — for parts of the West Bank. Check your government's advice and local conditions daily.

source.name: UK FCDO — travel advice for the Occupied Palestinian Territories

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official seasonal guidance. The CIA World Factbook describes the West Bank's climate as temperate, with warm to hot summers and cool to mild winters, and temperature and rainfall that vary with altitude.

idp.text: Palestine is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Palestine is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Palestine yet.

tips.text: There is no Palestinian visa. Entry is governed entirely by Israel. Travelers reach the West Bank through Ben Gurion Airport or the Allenby (King Hussein) Bridge from Jordan, passing Israeli immigration in both cases.

Admission is at Israel's discretion. The UK says you may face extra questioning at the border, and that some travellers entering at the Allenby Bridge or Ben Gurion Airport have been given stamps restricting them to 'Palestinian Authority only' or 'Judea and Samaria only'. Allow extra time.
Gaza is closed to travellers. The UK says border crossings out of Gaza have been closed to civilians and general traffic since the Israeli military took control of the Rafah crossing on 6 May 2024.

Movement within the West Bank passes through Israeli checkpoints. The UK says to keep your entry card with your passport until you leave, as you may need it when crossing into Palestine; expect delays.
Security conditions can deteriorate with little warning. Register with your embassy where possible and monitor its advice throughout your trip.

faq.question: Do I need a visa to visit Palestine?
faq.answer: The Palestinian Authority issues no visas and operates no border control, so entry is governed by Israel's rules. Nationalities that are visa-exempt for Israel — the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia and many others — need Israel's ETA-IL electronic travel authorization before flying; other nationalities need an Israeli visa from an embassy. Whatever admits you into Israel also covers onward travel to most of the West Bank.

faq.question: How do I get to the West Bank?
faq.answer: Either fly into Israel's Ben Gurion Airport and travel overland, or cross from Jordan over the Allenby (King Hussein) Bridge. Both routes pass Israeli border control.

faq.question: Can tourists visit Gaza?
faq.answer: No. The UK says border crossings out of Gaza have been closed to civilians and general traffic since the Israeli military took control of the Rafah crossing on 6 May 2024, and that consular support is not available inside Gaza.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Palestinian cities?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether, or where, Israeli citizens may enter the West Bank or Gaza. Check with the Israeli authorities before you travel.

faq.question: Will visiting the West Bank leave a stamp in my passport?
faq.answer: Not if you fly in: the UK says visitors entering through Ben Gurion Airport get an entry card instead of a passport stamp, while other crossings may give a card or a stamp. Keep the card with your passport until you leave.
